clue.text: Detectives appeal with certain anger

blocks.note: DIs are Detective Inspectors
a plea is an appeal
sure means certain

explanation.surface: Police officers make a plea while visibly furious about something.
explanation.definitionFit: Displeasure is annoyance or irritation, a milder synonym for anger.

clue.text: Household item oddly released odours with new fitting mounted

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters are let go, so only the even-placed ones of the next word stay
in a down clue, mounting means climbing upwards, so the letters read bottom to top

blocks.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of odours
N is the abbreviation for new
apt means fitting

explanation.surface: A household gadget leaks smells once a new part is installed.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the new-plus-fitting pair is mounted; the odours remnant stays the right way up at the top of the light.
explanation.definitionFit: A dustpan is a common domestic implement for sweeping up dirt, so it is a household item.

clue.text: Small number abandoned by leader becoming annoyed

indicators.note: being abandoned by its leader means the word loses its first letter

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
thirty is a number

explanation.surface: A small band of followers, deserted by their chief, grows irritated.
explanation.walkthrough: Shirty is informal British slang for bad-tempered.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone shirty is irritable or cross, the colloquial equivalent of annoyed.

clue.text: Delicate operation cladding outside of hero's tower

indicators.note: the outside of a word is its outermost letters, first and last

blocks.note: light means delicate, as a light touch
the first and last letters of hero
use means operation, as in 'in use'

explanation.surface: A delicate rescue mission surrounds the tower where the hero is.
explanation.walkthrough: USE clads, or attaches to the outside of, HO, giving LIGHT + HO + USE.
explanation.definitionFit: A lighthouse is a tall tower carrying a beacon to warn shipping.

clue.text: Water collected in seaquake

indicators.note: collected in says the letters are gathered inside the following word

blocks.note: the letters sit inside letters 3-6 of 'seaquake'

explanation.surface: Seawater gathers during an undersea earthquake.
explanation.definitionFit: Aqua is the Latin for water, used in English in that sense.

clue.text: Five in university once, all regularly avoiding ambiguity

indicators.note: regularly means taking letters at fixed intervals, here every other one

blocks.note: UNIV is a standard abbreviation for university, with V the Roman five ending it
first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: A group of five students at college once all steered clear of vague answers.
explanation.definitionFit: Univocal means having only one meaning, so such language leaves no ambiguity.

clue.text: Most nervous steed buckled carrying US soldier

indicators.note: something buckled is bent out of shape, so its letters are rearranged
carrying means holding something inside

blocks.note: taken as written
a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: The jumpiest horse collapsed under an American soldier rider.
explanation.walkthrough: GI goes inside the rearranged ED-EST.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgy means tense or nervous, so edgiest is its superlative.

clue.text: Juliet at ease, ignoring Romeo's teasing

indicators.note: ignoring a letter means leaving it out of the word

blocks.note: Juliet is J in the NATO alphabet
resting means relaxed, at ease
Romeo is R in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: Juliet relaxes and disregards Romeo's mockery.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface borrows Shakespeare's lovers, but both names are just radio-alphabet letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Jesting is joking or making fun, the same as teasing.

clue.text: Model on call joins actress

indicators.note: to model is to shape, so these letters are moulded into a new form

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A model who is on call joins an actress on set.
explanation.walkthrough: Joan Collins is the British actress famous for Dynasty.
explanation.definitionFit: Joan Collins is a well-known film and television star, so an example of an actress.

clue.text: Going through middle of pound with stray dog brought back

indicators.note: the middle of a word is its central letter
brought back means turned to face the other way, read right to left

blocks.note: the central letter of pound
to sin is to stray from virtue
a pug is a breed of dog

explanation.surface: A trip to the dog pound to collect a stray that is being returned.
explanation.definitionFit: Using up means consuming or exhausting, as going through supplies does.

clue.text: Construction tools Greek character conveyed on waterways

blocks.note: pi is a Greek letter
led means conveyed or guided
rivers are waterways

explanation.surface: Building equipment carried by a Greek along canals and rivers.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' places the first pieces above RIVERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Pile-drivers are machines that hammer posts into the ground, used on building sites.

clue.text: Father retired with little desire

indicators.note: to retire is to withdraw or go back, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: pa is an informal word for father
petite means small, little

explanation.surface: A dad who has stopped working now wants very little.
explanation.definitionFit: Appetite is a craving or longing, so a synonym for desire.

clue.text: Bots endlessly seen in tech company - is that so?

indicators.note: without ends means the first and last letters are dropped, leaving the core
seen in puts these letters inside another word

blocks.note: Bots without its first and last letters
Dell is a computer manufacturer

explanation.surface: Someone hears that automated bots are turning up at a tech firm and asks if it's true.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Do tell' is an idiom of interested or ironic surprise, inviting more, like 'is that so?'

clue.text: Zulu chief with bran scattered for stripy bird

indicators.note: scattered things are thrown about, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: Zulu is Z in the NATO alphabet
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Zulu chief scatters bran as feed for a striped bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The zebra finch is a small Australian finch named for its black-and-white barred markings.

clue.text: Turning, almost hit nose

indicators.note: almost means not quite complete, so the final letter goes
turning round means the letters are read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: to knock is to hit

explanation.surface: A boxer swivels and nearly lands a punch on the nose.
explanation.walkthrough: Conk is British slang for the nose; it also means hit, which adds to the trap.
explanation.definitionFit: Conk is a jocular slang word for a person's nose.

clue.text: Warning editor about participants for show being predicted

indicators.note: about means surrounding, going round the next piece

blocks.note: fore is the golfer's warning shout
ED is the abbreviation for editor
the cast are the performers in a show

explanation.surface: An editor is warned that the show's line-up has already been guessed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' means the warning and the editor, joined, go round the participants. Fore is the shout golfers give to warn of an incoming ball.
explanation.definitionFit: To forecast is to predict, so forecasted is a past-tense form of predicted.

clue.text: Attempt snooker shot that's crazy

blocks.note: a crack is an attempt, as in 'have a crack'
a pot sinks a ball in snooker

explanation.surface: Trying an insane shot at the snooker table.
explanation.definitionFit: Crackpot is an informal adjective for eccentric or mad ideas, the same as crazy.

clue.text: Most recent holiday destination that's used in desperation

definitions.note: read with 'that's' as 'something that's used in desperation', a noun phrase

blocks.note: last means latest, most recent
a resort is a place people go on holiday

explanation.surface: The newest holiday spot is the one chosen only when nothing else works.
explanation.definitionFit: A last resort is the final option, turned to only when all others have failed.

clue.text: Sisters on vacation eating top meals

indicators.note: vacated means emptied, so only the outer letters stay
eating takes something inside

blocks.note: Sisters with all its inner letters removed
upper means top, as in the upper deck

explanation.surface: Nuns on holiday enjoy first-rate dinners.
explanation.definitionFit: Suppers are evening meals.

clue.text: Shop very lacking in supply

indicators.note: lacking means missing, so these letters are taken out

blocks.note: taken as written
a delivery is a supply of goods

explanation.surface: A shop that is short of stock.
explanation.definitionFit: A deli, short for delicatessen, is a shop selling cooked meats and fine foods.

clue.text: Food beside nuts covering top of loaf

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter
nuts means crazy, so these letters are scrambled
covering means wrapping round something

blocks.note: taken as written
first letter of loaf

explanation.surface: Bread sits next to a bowl of nuts on the table, the nuts on top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nuts' looks like food, but it signals a jumble of BESIDE, which then wraps round L.
explanation.definitionFit: Edibles are things fit to be eaten, that is, food.

clue.text: Gold ship that is coming from big island

blocks.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
SS stands for steamship
i.e. abbreviates id est, 'that is'

explanation.surface: A ship carrying gold arrives from a huge island.
explanation.definitionFit: Aussie means Australian, and Australia is often called the world's largest island.

clue.text: Strong effect of deed on goblin

blocks.note: an imp is a mischievous goblin
an act is a deed

explanation.surface: A powerful result arising from a goblin's action.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue, 'A on B' conventionally puts A after B.
explanation.definitionFit: An impact is a marked influence or powerful effect.

clue.text: Very loud American, one hugged by First Lady gushing

indicators.note: being hugged means being held inside someone's arms

blocks.note: Eve is the first woman in Genesis
ff is fortissimo in music
US means American
I is the Roman one

explanation.surface: A loud American is embraced by the President's wife in a gushing welcome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First Lady' looks like a President's wife, but here it is the Bible's first woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Effusive means pouring out feeling without restraint, which is gushing.

clue.text: Bereft losing every third argument

indicators.note: losing every third means dropping the letters at positions three and six

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone heartbroken has lost a third of every quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Beef is slang for a grievance or quarrel, so an argument.

clue.text: Adjusted telescope after missing company's tall structure

indicators.note: adjusted means altered, so these letters are rearranged
missing means taking the next piece out of the word

blocks.note: taken as written
CO is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A telescope set up to view a firm's tall building.
explanation.definitionFit: A steeple is the tall pointed tower of a church.

clue.text: Settles comfortably within finest lesson

indicators.note: within says the letters lie inside the phrase that follows

blocks.note: the letters run across letters 3-9 of 'finest lesson'

explanation.surface: A pupil relaxes into the best class ever.
explanation.definitionFit: To nestle is to snuggle down into a cosy position.

clue.text: Car not entirely activated with parts of feet

indicators.note: not entirely means incomplete, so the final letter is lost

blocks.note: set off means triggered or activated
W is an abbreviation for with
heels are the back parts of the feet

explanation.surface: A car started only partly, with someone's feet doing the work.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Set of wheels' is informal slang for a car.
